proposed_from.topic: Gaussian-free residual-law identification of all interventions in confounded additive-noise SCMs under an exact intervention cover. For a known acyclic treatment DAG with X_i=f_i(X_Pa(i))+U_i and Y=f_Y(X)+U_Y, allow an arbitrary correlated Borel disturbance law with finite second moments. Given the full observational law, do(X=x), and a fixed finite regime collection R whose families leave each i free while intervening on all Pa(i), require coverage of the entire observational support and every recursively reached target support. Prove that regime means identify every structural mean, observational residuals identify the complete centered joint exogenous law, and a topological residual pushforward identifies every covered postintervention distribution and bounded AOI. Prove the same exact combinatorial cover is necessary for universal identification by two bounded non-Gaussian SCMs that agree simultaneously on the complete regime tuple but differ on a target intervention. Construct a cross-fitted regime-regression plus joint-residual-resampling estimator with bootstrap inference for smooth AOIs and distributional bands under explicit no-atom/density conditions. Use the four-point Rademacher residual witness and Jeunen et al.'s published International Stroke Trial semi-synthetic intervention-disentanglement benchmark; do not claim a new clinical aspirin conclusion.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest result of Elahi, Ghasemi, and Kocaoglu characterizes hard parent covers for Gaussian average outcomes. The closest soft-intervention identification theory of Correa and Bareinboim gives graphical calculi for stochastic policies and transportability. Neither result states a functional rank condition under which finitely many natural-value shifts recover nonlinear additive mechanisms, the complete dependent disturbance law, and all hard-intervention distributions, nor supplies a same-regime-tuple bounded witness when that rank fails.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Theorem 2 and Appendix A.3 give a Gaussian mean-level parent-cover result; equations (3)--(15) reveal that Gaussianity first enters when conditional disturbance means are reduced to covariances, while equation (9) already identifies centered mechanisms from regime means.
seed_details.kernel: Prove that exact recursive support coverage identifies the complete centered disturbance law and every postintervention law, and is universally necessary via two bounded four-point non-Gaussian SCMs.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After mechanism recovery, replace Gaussian covariance reconstruction and conditional means by the observational vector-residual pushforward.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches pairing confounded additive noise with full intervention distributions, arbitrary dependent noise, residual-law recovery, and parent covers returned no closer theorem than the Gaussian mean papers.
seed_details.red_team: The result is immediate from Elahi, Ghasemi, and Kocaoglu because their proof already reconstructs residuals.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their theorem targets means, reconstructs Gaussian covariance, and its necessity changes a mechanism on a probability-zero set; full-law recovery and a bounded four-point simultaneous-regime witness require different arguments.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The kernel is an explicit if-and-only-if functional with a non-Gaussian region and matching witness, not sufficient-only identification.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Section 4 alternates likelihood fitting with Gaussian covariance estimation, and the conclusion leaves non-Gaussian noise open; no functional CLT or simultaneous band is supplied.
seed_details.kernel: Derive the influence function and exchangeable-bootstrap limit for cross-fitted regime regressions followed by joint residual resampling and recursive intervention propagation.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the Gaussian likelihood covariance update by an empirical joint residual law and linearize its repeated recursive appearances.
seed_details.target_method_search: Chernozhukov, Fernández-Val, and Melly treat regression counterfactual distributions, but searches found no generated joint-residual recursion across intervention regimes.
seed_details.red_team: This is a routine functional delta-method corollary of counterfactual distribution regression.
seed_details.rebuttal: The same estimated residual vector enters every recursion and is generated from several fitted mechanisms, so its influence and bootstrap coupling are absent from the published operator.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The proposal names a primitive local-polynomial learner and a joint bootstrap handle rather than assuming nuisance rates or a CLT.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Theorem 2 stops at interventional means; once centered mechanisms and the common residual vector are recovered, the same disturbance draw can couple factual and nested worlds.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize exactly which factual-conditioned and nested counterfactual laws are identified by abduction through the observed residual fiber followed by covered actions.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After residual recovery, disintegrate the residual law on factual fibers before applying counterfactual unnesting.
seed_details.target_method_search: Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim characterize graph-only nested identification, but no located result combines their factors with intervention-cover mechanism recovery.
seed_details.red_team: Once an SCM is recovered, counterfactual identification is tautological.
seed_details.rebuttal: Only centered mechanisms and a residual law are recovered; regular conditional residual laws on factual fibers and support-specific necessity remain nontrivial and can fail at null fibers.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The target is a cross-world law with a new residual-coupling functional, not ordinary do-calculus.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Theorem 2 requires parent exposure and does not characterize missing assignment values; Appendix A.3 uses a point change to prove failure.
seed_details.kernel: Give sharp recursively compatible CDF and AOI bounds when uncovered mechanisms obey directional-derivative envelopes.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace exact regime-mean evaluation at the first missing parent value by upper and lower extrapolation envelopes, then optimize them jointly through the common residual recursion.
seed_details.target_method_search: Pfister and Bühlmann provide single-function extrapolation bounds, but no search result propagated compatible envelopes through a confounded SCM residual law.
seed_details.red_team: The bounds follow by independently plugging nodewise Lipschitz intervals into the DAG.
seed_details.rebuttal: Independent extrema need not share one residual law or one globally compatible descendant mechanism, so sharpness requires a coupled extremal construction.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The natural object is a coupled pushforward envelope, not an unspecified LP.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Equation (17) exposes a mechanism because hard interventions hold every parent fixed; this first step fails under soft changes that leave parental variation.
seed_details.kernel: Derive a necessary-and-sufficient operator-rank condition on known soft regimes for baseline mechanism and residual-law recovery.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace direct regime-mean revelation by inversion of regime-contrast integral operators.
seed_details.target_method_search: Soft-intervention identification papers characterize graphical transport or graph equivalence, not a full-law rank cover for dependent-noise ANMs.
seed_details.red_team: Known soft kernels can be rewritten as mixtures of hard interventions, making the result immediate.
seed_details.rebuttal: Mixture inversion can be noninjective, and the exact rank frontier must also recover the common dependent residual coupling.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The focal object is an operator-rank iff frontier rather than a relabeled hard cover.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Theorem 3 combines randomized intervention selection with graph recovery under Gaussian noise, while the full mechanism argument still presumes the recovered parent sets.
seed_details.kernel: Recover the treatment DAG, centered mechanisms, and dependent non-Gaussian residual law with a polylogarithmic separating design.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Gaussian dependence tests in the edge-exposure stage by invariance of regime-mean contrasts across candidate parent-fixing environments.
seed_details.target_method_search: Arbitrary-noise ANM discovery results require independent errors, and latent-variable intervention designs do not recover nonlinear mechanisms or their joint residual law.
seed_details.red_team: Elahi, Ghasemi, and Kocaoglu already recover the graph with polylogarithmically many regimes.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their orientation and effect recovery are Gaussian; correlated arbitrary noise destroys observational ANM factorization and demands a new interventional invariance step.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is a mechanism-recovery problem under structural indeterminacy, so it uses M18 rather than effect identification alone.

seed_details.opened_evidence: The randomized design counts intervention target sets but does not optimize assignment values needed to cover recursive supports of a specified target class.
seed_details.kernel: Choose a minimum-cost finite regime-and-assignment family that satisfies exact recursive support cover, with an approximation certificate for continuous supports discretized by a target tolerance.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace node-only set cover by a hypergraph whose elements are node--parent-value cells generated recursively by target interventions.
seed_details.target_method_search: Kandasamy et al. optimize graph-level do-calculus covers; no located paper optimizes value-specific ANM support covers.
seed_details.red_team: This is ordinary weighted set cover after enumerating parent values.
seed_details.rebuttal: The universe is endogenous because intervention choices change recursively reached supports; the certificate must couple design and reachability rather than cover a fixed list.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The design is the decision variable and requires an optimality certificate.

seed_details.opened_evidence: The paper extrapolates unseen intervention combinations parametrically but provides no robustness index for small uncovered support regions under non-Gaussian noise.
seed_details.kernel: Define the smallest recursively reached uncovered mass at which a sign conclusion for a bounded AOI can reverse, and derive sharp sensitivity envelopes as a function of that mass and a Lipschitz radius.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace exact residual pushforward at uncovered cells by a contamination coupling whose mass is amplified along descendants.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches found extrapolation bounds for one regression but no critical uncovered-mass scalar for a recursive confounded ANM.
seed_details.red_team: The critical mass is just total-variation contamination sensitivity.
seed_details.rebuttal: Descendant recursion and a common residual vector create graph-dependent amplification, so the sign frontier is not the marginal contamination radius.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: A valid version must derive both envelopes and a critical sign-reversal mass; qualitative robustness would be rejected.
